chunks: And ʿAbd al-Wāḥid ibn al-Mukhtār al-Anṣārī narrated from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about the Duḥā prayer, so he said: “The first ones to perform it were your people. Indeed, they were among the heedless, so they perform it; and the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله did not perform it.”

And he said: “Indeed, ʿAlī عليه السلام passed by a man while he was performing it, so ʿAlī عليه السلام said: ‘What is this prayer?’ He said: ‘Should I leave it, O Amīr al-Muʾminīn?’ He عليه السلام said: ‘Would I forbid a servant when he prays?’”

key_terms.أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful, a title of Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام
key_terms.الْغَافِلِينَ: the heedless; those described here as inattentive or unaware
key_terms.رَسُولُ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
key_terms.صَلَاةِ الضُّحَى: the Duḥā prayer, a supererogatory prayer performed in the forenoon

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about Ṣalāt al-Ḍuḥā and whether the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم or Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام performed or approved it?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses Ṣalāt al-Ḍuḥā and states that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم did not perform it. It also recounts that Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام questioned a man praying it, yet did not explicitly forbid him from praying, indicating a nuanced legal and devotional context.
